chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, who said:

A woman asked me to seek permission for her from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), so I sought permission for her. She entered, and with her was a slave-girl of hers. She said, 'O Abū ʿAbdillāh! What is meant by the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'A olive-tree, neither of the East nor of the West'?' He said, 'O woman! Indeed, Allah did not strike the examples for the tree; rather, He struck the examples for the Children of Adam. Ask what you intend.'

She said, 'Inform me about the lesbian with the lesbian, what is their legal punishment (ḥadd) regarding it?' He said, 'The legal punishment of adultery. Indeed, when it is the Day of Resurrection, they will be brought having been dressed in garments cut from Fire, veiled with veils of Fire, and wearing trousers of Fire, and pillars of Fire will be inserted into their bellies up to their heads, and they will be thrown into the Fire. O woman! The first people to perform this act were the people of Lūṭ. The men sufficed themselves with the men, so the women remained without men, so they did as their men had done.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal punishment for lesbianism in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'olive tree' in Surah An-Nur is a metaphor for human beings rather than botanical entities, emphasizing the allegorical nature of Quranic parables. He further details the eschatological punishment for lesbianism, describing a specific torment involving garments and pillars of fire, and attributes the origin of this act to the People of Lot, noting how men's preference for men left women to emulate the behavior. This narration provides both exegetical insight into Quranic imagery and jurisprudential context regarding the *hadd* (fixed punishment) for female same-sex relations in Shia tradition.
